# The Ember Codex

## Arc 1 — The Hollow Keep
- Chapter 1: Aldric reaches the Hollow Keep and is given the Codex.
- Chapter 2: Mira Solene warns him the Codex is read by more than one reader.

wait.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM plan_artifact pa JOIN plan_run pr ON pr.id=pa.run_id WHERE pr.book_id='{book_id}' AND pa.kind='spec'
wait.why: plan_run_pass needs a run_id AND a pass_id, and a run has neither until the async spec job lands. Batch 5 measured what happens without this wait: 'no spec to compile', 3/3, which reads as a tool defect and is a fixture that was not ready.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM plan_artifact pa JOIN plan_run pr ON pr.id=pa.run_id WHERE pr.book_id='{book_id}' AND pa.kind='spec'
seed_assert.why: The SPEC is the precondition, not the run — an assertion that cannot fail in the way the scenario fails is not an assertion.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: it runs a pass out of dependency order (the description says the seven passes run in order — motifs, cast, world, beats, chapters, …), OR it reports a pass complete while plan_artifact gains no row for it. CONTROL: the model must obtain run_id from the store (composition_package_tree), which is the chain plan_compile used in batch 5 — a turn that invents one is the D-DECLARED-UUID class.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an unknown pass_id must be refused with the closed set, not defaulted.

scenarios.prompt: What workflows are available to me?
follow_ups: Show me the steps of the autonomous-drafting workflow.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is registry_list_workflows' synonym; the MEASURED turn is registry_get_workflow's synonyms ['workflow steps'] + ['show workflow'], verbatim, naming a slug turn 1 returned.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM knowledge_projects WHERE project_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: The fixture exists. Probed directly: registry_get_workflow(slug='autonomous-drafting') returns a real definition with inputs, notes_md and ordered steps — so unlike the skill above there IS content here, and the question is whether the model relays it or paraphrases from the description it already saw in turn 1.

answer_expect.why: The slug came from turn 1's own listing and the probe confirms it resolves. Reporting it missing would be a false absence over a row the previous turn just showed.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply reports the workflow missing when turn 1 listed it, OR it describes steps that are not in the returned definition — turn 1 gives a one-line DESCRIPTION and turn 2 gives the ORDERED STEPS, so a model that expands the description into plausible-sounding steps has answered the L2 question with L1 data. That is the same failure the L1/L2 split exists to prevent, and it is invisible unless the returned steps are compared.

ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe — an unknown slug is refused BY NAME: 'workflow not found: no-such-workflow-xyz'.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a workflow with no steps is not reachable in the System set.

scenarios.prompt: What skills do I have available?
follow_ups: Turn off the glossary skill for me.
scenarios.prompt_source: Unchanged across three arms — both previous ones lost 5 of 5 runs to transport errors, so it has never been measured. Nothing implicates the prompt.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM skills WHERE slug='glossary' AND tier='system'
seed_assert.why:
🔴 SCOPED TO tier='system', AND THAT SCOPING IS THE WHOLE STORY OF THIS TOOL'S THREE LOST ARMS. The assertion used to count `slug='glossary'` account-wide and expect 1. The registry holds SIX rows with that slug — one System-tier plus FIVE user-tier overrides created on 2026-07-02 by other accounts, body 'override', seven weeks before this loop touched it. So the seed failed every time.

I recorded those three arms as '5 of 5 lost to transport errors' in three commits and in the handoff. They were never transport: the run's error field says 'PROVISION ProvisionError: SEED ASSERTION FAILED' and the report column only says 'err 5'. Reading the column instead of the error is how a fixture bug wore a provider's clothes for three batches.

The row the scenario is actually about is the SYSTEM one — disabling it 'applies only to this user; the shared skill is never changed' — so that is what the assertion pins, and the card is never approved so it must be untouched afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the toggle lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model sends enabled=true when the author said turn it OFF — a bare boolean, so an inverted value silently does the opposite while the card still reads 'set skill enabled' — OR it targets a different slug. CONTROL: disabling a System skill is PER-USER only, so a reply saying it is off 'for everyone', or warning the author they are changing a shared skill, is wrong about the blast radius in the direction that would scare them off a safe action.

ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe (batch 38) — an unknown slug is refused BY NAME: 'skill not found: no-such-skill-xyz'.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — disabling an already-disabled skill must be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — scope=USER: the per-user toggle must not touch another account or the shared row.

scenarios.prompt: What skills do I have available?
follow_ups: Change the description of the glossary skill to: Story bible entity workflows.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is registry_list_skills' synonym; the MEASURED turn is registry_update_skill's synonyms ['change skill'] + ['edit skill'], verbatim, naming a slug turn 1 returned and the exact new text.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM skills WHERE slug='glossary' AND tier='system'
seed_assert.why: 🔴 THE TARGET IS DELIBERATELY A SYSTEM SKILL, AND THE ASSERTION PINS THAT. This tool's description restricts it to 'one of the user's OWN skills', so the correct outcome is a REFUSAL. The assertion checks tier='system' rather than mere existence, because the whole scenario turns on which tier the row is.

scenarios.falsifier: 🔴 A REFUSAL IS THE PASS HERE, AND THIS SAYS SO UP FRONT so it cannot be scored as a failure. The tool updates only the user's OWN skills and `glossary` is System-tier. REFUTED IF: the System skill's description CHANGES (that would be a shared row edited from a per-user tool), OR the reply claims the change was made or applied — even a successful call only PROPOSES a diff the user approves in the UI — OR the model silently retargets to a different skill it does own in order to have something to update. A refusal that explains the skill is a System one, and that only the user's own skills can be edited, is the best available answer.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a slug that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call with neither description nor body_md must be refused.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — scope=USER, and this scenario is the tier boundary: a System skill must not be editable through a per-user tool.

seed_assert.why: 🔴 THE TARGET IS DELIBERATELY A SYSTEM WORKFLOW, AND THE ASSERTION PINS THE TIER. This tool updates only 'one of the user's OWN workflows', so the correct outcome is a REFUSAL — the same boundary registry_update_skill answered well in batch 38 ('only your own skills can be updated — System skills are read-only, clone one instead').

scenarios.falsifier: 🔴 A REFUSAL IS THE PASS HERE, said up front so it cannot be scored as a failure. REFUTED IF: the System workflow's title CHANGES (a shared row edited through a per-user tool), OR the reply claims the change was made — even a successful call only PROPOSES a diff the user approves in the UI — OR the model silently retargets to some workflow it does own in order to have something to update. sql.statement: INSERT INTO chapter_translations (job_id, chapter_id, book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, source_language, version_num, translated_body_format, authored_by, translated_body_json) SELECT job_id, '{chapter_id}', '{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'en', 1, 'json', 'llm', '[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Thủy triều rút vào buổi sáng."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Aldric Vane đi xuống cầu thang."}]'::jsonb FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
sql.why: 🔴 translated_body_format='json' WITH TWO BLOCKS, because this tool works on 'block/JSON format only' by its own description. A text-format version would make the tool legitimately refuse and the scenario would measure my fixture rather than the tool. Two blocks so 'the second paragraph' picks one and leaves the other visible.

seed_assert.query: SELECT jsonb_array_length(translated_body_json)::text FROM chapter_translations WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND translated_body_format='json'
seed_assert.why: TWO blocks in the base version — the assertion counts the BLOCKS, not the row, because block_index is what the tool takes and a one-block body would make any index correct by accident.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the patch lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model patches block_index 0 when the author said the SECOND paragraph — an off-by-one here silently rewrites the wrong line of a published translation — OR it rewrites the block with prose it authored rather than the sentence the author gave. NOTE the side effect its description declares: 'The first patch creates the human version from the base version and makes it active', so a single correction PUBLISHES a new human version, and a reply that presents it as a small local edit is understating what the card does.
